notes: Ground delivery robots and driverless delivery vehicles as of 11 Nov 2026, one marker per city per operator. Starship ended US campus service in mid-2026 so those sites are omitted; China, Finland and campus fleets are far larger than the markers shown, and about 20 US states with no located statute are left as no data.

ARE.summary: Dubai and Abu Dhabi license delivery robots and driverless delivery vans; Yango robots are cleared for public walkways.

AUS.summary: Delivery robots are not automatically legal and rely on local approval; the first footpath service began on the Gold Coast in 2026.

AUT.summary: Trials only: Zelos completed its first European unmanned delivery vehicle deployment in Linz.

BEL.summary: Trials only: Collect&Go tested a remotely supervised Clevon vehicle in Leuven in 2026; full autonomy is not yet permitted.

CAN.summary: City by city: Toronto banned sidewalk robots in 2021, while Vancouver approved a six-month Serve Robotics pilot in May 2026.

CHE.summary: Driverless delivery vans run as pilots: LOXO and Planzer operate an automated parcel van on public roads in Bern.

CHN.summary: Unmanned delivery vans run at scale under city road-rights permits; ZTO alone reports 3,500 vehicles in 268 cities.

CZE.summary: No dedicated law found; foodora and Starship began the first Czech sidewalk robot pilot in Prague 8 in December 2025.

DEU.summary: German law has no vehicle category for delivery robots; operations such as Starship and REWE in Hamburg run as pilots.

EST.summary: A 2017 Traffic Act change created a self-driving delivery robot category (6 km/h on sidewalks); Starship delivers in Tallinn.

FIN.summary: Sidewalk robots operate nationwide: Starship and S Group run 650-plus robots in about 80 towns, with no licence scheme.

GBR.summary: Pavement robots sit in a legal grey area: the government has approved none but plans a lawful route, and trials run in several towns.

JPN.summary: Since April 2023 the Road Traffic Act lets small remote-operated robots use sidewalks after police notification; Rakuten runs a service.

KOR.summary: Since November 2023 safety-certified outdoor robots count as pedestrians on sidewalks; Baemin and Neubility run delivery.

LTU.summary: Clevon holds permits to run its driverless carriers on public roads and delivered groceries for IKI in Vilnius.

SAU.summary: Trials only: the Transport General Authority runs pilot schemes for delivery robots and driverless parcel vehicles in Riyadh.

SGP.summary: Trials only: robots need LTA approval for public paths, with a precinct-wide testbed in Punggol Digital District from 2026.

SWE.summary: Delivery robots run under trial permits from the Transport Agency (Ordinance 2017:309); foodora and Starship test in Stockholm.

US-AR.summary: Act HB1767 of 2021 added a personal delivery device subchapter to the traffic code, with a $100,000 insurance requirement.

US-AZ.summary: ARS 28-1222 gives delivery robots pedestrian rules statewide; DoorDash Dot and Waymo vehicles deliver in metro Phoenix.

US-CA.summary: No statewide sidewalk-robot statute: cities permit or pause robots (Glendale moratorium, 2026); services run in LA and San Jose.

US-CO.summary: Listed among states that have legalised personal delivery devices; no public robot delivery service found.

US-DC.summary: The District permits personal delivery devices under DDOT rules; Serve and Coco began DoorDash deliveries in 2026.

US-FL.summary: Statute 316.2071 allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks with insurance; Serve and Coco run commercial delivery in Miami.

US-GA.summary: State law permits personal delivery devices; a 2026 act raised the sidewalk speed limit to 7 mph. Serve operates in Atlanta.

US-IA.summary: Iowa Code chapter 321O (2021) authorises personal delivery devices on roads and sidewalks, capped at 6 mph on sidewalks.

US-ID.summary: State law allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks and crosswalks; no public robot delivery service found.

US-IL.summary: No state statute; Chicago runs a licensed sidewalk robot pilot with Coco and Serve that ends after May 2027 without council action.

US-IN.summary: Indiana Code 9-21-11.5 permits personal delivery devices that carry an identifier and a controlled-stop system.

US-KS.summary: SB 161 (2022) authorises personal delivery devices, excludes them from the vehicle definition and sets a $50 annual fee.

US-LA.summary: A 2021 law allows delivery devices at 12 mph in pedestrian areas and 20 mph elsewhere; parishes and cities may ban them.

US-MA.summary: No state statute: personal delivery device bill H.3331 died in 2024 and later bills have not passed.

US-MD.summary: Chapter 351 of 2021 authorises personal delivery devices with marking, insurance and operator requirements.

US-MO.summary: Rev. Stat. 304.900 authorises personal delivery devices on sidewalks, crosswalks and roadways and limits local regulation.

US-MS.summary: Miss. Code 63-3-1331 recognises personal delivery devices and exempts them from motor vehicle laws.

US-NC.summary: G.S. 20-175.16 allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks at up to 10 mph with a remote operator; cities may restrict them.

US-NJ.summary: No state statute; Jersey City and Hoboken allow sidewalk robots under city-run pilot programmes.

US-NV.summary: SB 422 (2023) allows personal delivery devices in limited places such as state university campuses.

US-NY.summary: No framework: bills S9950 and A10766 to create a personal delivery device permit were introduced in 2026 but not enacted.

US-OH.summary: State law allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks; Avride and Grubhub run about 120 robots at Ohio State University.

US-OK.summary: Oklahoma has approved autonomous sidewalk delivery devices by state law.

US-PA.summary: Act 106 of 2020 regulates delivery robots as pedestrians, up to 550 lb; Avride robots deliver in Philadelphia.

US-TN.summary: A 2026 law lets delivery robots use bike paths and road shoulders at up to 20 mph; Knoxville bans them downtown.

US-TX.summary: Transportation Code chapter 552A (2019) lets businesses run delivery robots under pedestrian rules; Serve and Avride operate here.

US-UT.summary: State law allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks and crosswalks; no public robot delivery service found.

US-VA.summary: First state to legalise personal delivery devices on sidewalks (2017); Serve and Avride robots now serve Alexandria and Arlington.

US-WA.summary: A 2019 law (RCW 46.75) allows registered personal delivery devices on sidewalks and crosswalks with human oversight.

US-WI.summary: State law allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks and crosswalks; Starship ended its UW-Madison campus service in 2026.

US-WV.summary: W. Va. Code 17C-24 allows personal delivery devices on sidewalks and crosswalks with an ID marker and operator contact details.

USA.summary: No federal sidewalk-robot law: states and cities set the rules, and commercial robot delivery runs in more than a dozen metro areas.
